default.p.test-1-p1.vietnamese:
Calisthenics is a form of gentle exercise performed before beginning formal sports activities. At school, even when the physical education teacher teaches with all their effort, the students’ ways of moving their bodies never become exactly the same. Viewed from behind, each person’s movements are slightly different. This is somewhat puzzling.

I think there are many possible reasons, but perhaps the students have not watched the teacher carefully. The problem may lie more in the way they learn, or take in information, than in the way they are taught.

From this small scene at school, I realized profoundly that nothing is more important than the ability to observe people and things.

default.p.test-10-p1.vietnamese:
Nowadays, cars are no longer what could be called convenient tools of civilization. Japan’s total population is approximately 125 million. The total number of automobiles—including passenger cars, buses, trucks, dump trucks, and tankers—is more than 80 million. Roughly speaking, there is one car for every 0.65 people—a truly astonishing figure.

If this continues, there may eventually be more cars than people. This enormous number of cars runs on the roads morning, noon, and night. The more cars there are, the more people are injured or killed in accidents each year. That is the reality today.

My daughter, who is in her third year of university, said that she wanted to take the driving test for a license. Half angry and half puzzled, I asked, “Why do you need one?” She replied, “Because all my friends have one.”

She had no real need for one, and we had no money to buy a car, so I could not understand why she insisted so strongly on getting a license. In particular, her university is extremely close; it takes less than ten minutes to walk there.

When I raised my voice slightly and said, “What basis is there for saying that just because your friends have one, you must have one too?” she bluntly replied, “Dad, you’re so old-fashioned!”

I knew that “old-fashioned” referred to someone who is out of touch with the changes of the times and has fallen behind, but honestly, being called “old-fashioned” by my own daughter simply because I did not have a driver’s license was not pleasant.

When I raised my voice even more and said, “Even if you get a license, where will you get the money to buy a car?”

She argued back, “I can work part-time to save the down payment first, and then take out a loan and pay in installments!”

I pressed her further: “Once you’re in debt and paying in installments, what will you use to repay it?”

She continued to argue: “I’ll graduate in another year. Once I start working, that amount won’t be a big deal!”

I myself do not feel that a license is entirely unnecessary, but I have no desire to take the driving test. That is because, more than the financial issue, I am afraid of having an accident because my motor skills and reflexes are slow.

Among my high school friends, only three people, including me, do not have a driver’s license. Those who do have one look thoroughly satisfied and say, “Having a car really is convenient. Don’t say you still don’t need one at your age—go get your license soon. If you get one now, life will be twice as enjoyable. A cheap mini-car wouldn’t be much of a burden. At most, you could start with an inexpensive used car. Don’t be so old-fashioned!”

I had just heard the word “old-fashioned” from my friends, and now even my own daughter was saying exactly the same thing. It made me seriously wonder whether I really was old-fashioned. However, I had heard another story at last month’s class reunion: “Kimura caused a car accident, and he’s having a terribly hard time now.” As long as stories like that continue to echo in my ears, I will certainly never get a driver’s license, and I console myself by thinking that I am fine as I am.

(Note 1) もはや: Before one realizes it; by now.

(Note 2) 利器: A convenient or useful device.

(Note 3) おびただしい: Astonishing, countless, extremely numerous.

(Note 4) 切り出す: To open a conversation or begin bringing up a matter for discussion.

(Note 5) 曰く: According to what someone says; reportedly.

(Note 6) うとい: To be poorly informed about; to be out of touch with.

(Note 7) 声高に: In a loud voice; loudly.

(Note 8) 頭金: A cash payment made in advance when entering into a contract.

default.p.test-11-p1.vietnamese:
All tours last 4 days and 3 nights, including the departure day.
All tours stay at Hotel ABC!

【Tour A】
Schedule: Daily departures from April 28 (Saturday) to May 3 (Thursday)
Description: Explore the profound history of Korea and its proud, long-standing traditions! Visit famous mountains, temples, and cultural sites within a 100-km radius of Seoul, including Seoul's royal palaces. On the final day, shop at Dongdaemun Market!
Estimated Departure & Arrival: Narita Airport 9:00 a.m. / Narita Airport 5:00 p.m.
Tour price: 44,800 yen

【Tour B】
Schedule: Daily departures from April 28 (Saturday) to May 2 (Wednesday)
Description: Enjoy a feast of culinary delights, including famous mountains, temples, Korean barbecue, and bibimbap, with Korea's cultural heritage at the center! In addition to shopping in Seoul's bustling districts, relax with an exceptional spa service in Gangnam!
Estimated Departure & Arrival: Narita Airport 9:00 a.m. / Haneda Airport 5:00 p.m.
Tour price: 40,000 yen

【Tour C】
Schedule: Only two departures, on April 28 and May 1
Description: Korea, the true home of Korean barbecue! Enjoy Jeonju bibimbap on the first day. On the second day, try Suwon grilled ribs—have you heard of them? The tour ends with a visit to Seoul's royal palaces, a walk through Myeongdong, and duty-free shopping! For mixed-gender couples traveling together, only the female guest may enjoy the ultimate spa package!
Estimated Departure & Arrival: Haneda Airport 7:00 a.m. / Haneda Airport 6:00 p.m.
Tour price: 47,000 yen

【Tour D】
Schedule: Only two departures, on May 1 and May 3
Description: Would you like to try singing the song “Return to Busan Port” in Busan, the Korean city closest to Japan? After Busan, a seafood paradise, visit the thousand-year-old former capital of Gyeongju. Gyeongju boasts countless cultural heritage sites! You cannot discuss Korea without first seeing Gyeongju! Spa service is naturally included in the tour.
Estimated Departure & Arrival: Narita Airport 9:00 a.m. / Narita Airport 5:00 p.m.
Tour price: 41,700 yen

【Tour E】
Schedule: Daily departures from April 28 (Saturday) to May 2 (Wednesday)
Description: Jeju Island is filled with breathtaking natural scenery across the entire island. Enjoy the striking contrast between the sea and Jeju, a dormant volcanic island. The sunset over this southern island will surely add color to your youth. Fresh seafood products brought in by the island's female divers. Countless caves with the mysterious beauty of nature. Waterfalls plunging down with tremendous force. This place will surely become part of your beautiful youth. Because you are lovers, you want to give it to each other. Because you are lovers, you want to share it with each other (Note 4).
Estimated Departure & Arrival: Narita Airport 9:00 a.m. / Narita Airport 5:00 p.m.
Tour price: 47,000 yen

【Tour F】
Schedule: Only two departures, on April 28 and May 1
Description: After visiting Jeju Island, filled with magnificent scenery everywhere, tour the Dadohae Archipelago. Visit the Baekje region, regarded as the source of Japan, and finish in Seoul. Relax with a princess-style spa service in Myeongdong. Hunt for and shop for Hallyu star merchandise at Dongdaemun Market (Note 5).
Estimated Departure & Arrival: Haneda Airport 5:00 a.m. / Narita Airport 7:00 p.m.
Tour price: 46,000 yen

*** Please see the website for detailed information about all tours.
*** Spa services are available to women only.

（Note 1）Gourmet: The sophisticated enjoyment of food and fine cuisine

（Note 2）Boyfriend: A male romantic partner

（Note 3）Plan: To think about and make plans to do something

（Note 4）Share with each other: To divide among one another and share together

（Note 5）Hunt for and shop: Searching everywhere and buying items in quantity

default.p.test-14-p1.vietnamese:
Every year, I ask my international students to write their answers to the question, "What is the first thing you think of when you hear Japan?" Until now, many answers had relatively positive associations, such as "friendly," "gentle," "developed country," "hardworking," "sumo," "Shinkansen," "baseball," and "ramen." However, at some point, negative words such as "listless," "disappointed," and "hopeless" began to reach my ears more often. This became especially noticeable after the Great East Japan Earthquake. I thought that the perspective of people coming from outside might be more accurate than that of people living inside Japan.

（Note 1）Sumo: A traditional Japanese sport in which two wrestlers compete by throwing down an opponent or pushing the opponent out of a circular ring of sand.

（Note 2）Kikoe no yoi: Affirmative or positive; pleasant or cheerful to hear.

（Note 3）Sōshitsu: Losing or being deprived of something.

default.p.test-15-p1.vietnamese:
Apparently, someone has researched walking speed. According to this person, Japanese people walk faster than almost anyone else in the world. There are many reasons why people walk quickly, but the number-one reason is 「because they are being chased by time」. When asked 「Why are you being chased by time?」, the most common answer was 「Because they stay up until late at night and sleep until just before it is time to get up in the morning」. default.p.test-17-p1.vietnamese:
People often say that stress is the source of all illness. I think that is probably true, but can we maintain a social life without experiencing any stress at all? Surely that is impossible.

Of all types of stress, workplace stress is undoubtedly the greatest. Some of it originates in relationships within the company, such as those between superiors and subordinates or between coworkers, while other stress comes from customers and business partners. Stress can also arise within the family. Marital arguments are probably a typical example.

Apparently, some people are less susceptible to stress, while others are said to be the type who easily experience and accumulate it, but stress itself is a cause of many different illnesses. Typical examples include cancer, heart disease, and diseases of the brain. In this situation, learning how to relieve excessive stress becomes the key to human happiness and longevity. I think it is important to have hobbies that one genuinely enjoys, but pursuing hobbies is difficult if one lacks the time and money.

Therefore, I recommend walking or doing stretching exercises that can be performed at home.

It is now the off-season for professional baseball, a sport that is currently very popular. All the players are in a period of individual training, working hard to build their basic physical fitness. Although I cannot train like them, I strongly feel that I want to build basic physical fitness in my own way so that I can become healthy both physically and mentally.

(Note 1) Excessive: so heavy or severe that it becomes too much

(Note 2) At just that moment: precisely at that time

(Note 3) Training independently: a period of voluntarily practicing on one's own

default.p.test-18-p1.outline.0.label: The meaning of one’s hometown and longing when away
default.p.test-18-p1.outline.0.note: Opens by quoting a poem by Muroo Saisei about one's hometown and defining a hometown as a place filled with memories and affection.
default.p.test-18-p1.outline.1.label: Memories of the scenery of Mount Tsukuba in the author's hometown
default.p.test-18-p1.outline.1.note: Describes the author’s hometown: a vast, flat plain with the imposing 877-meter-high Mount Tsukuba to the north, creating an unchanging composition in paintings. Question 1 is based on this passage.
default.p.test-18-p1.outline.2.label: Life away from home and feelings when meeting someone from the same hometown
default.p.test-18-p1.outline.2.note: The author has lived away from home for many years and lost touch with old friends, but upon meeting someone from the same hometown at a new company, hearing the familiar accent feels deeply comforting. Passage supporting Question 2.
default.p.test-18-p1.outline.3.label: The salmon's survival pattern and its connection to its origins
default.p.test-18-p1.outline.3.note: Relates salmon’s life cycle—being born, swimming out to the open sea, returning upstream to spawn, and dying—to people’s connection with their roots. The basis for Question 3 is found here.
default.p.test-18-p1.outline.4.label: Vocabulary notes in the passage
default.p.test-18-p1.outline.4.note: Explains difficult words, idioms, and place names appearing in the reading.
default.p.test-18-p1.vietnamese:
The famous poet Muroo Saisei once wrote in a poem, “One’s hometown is a place to remember when far away.” Perhaps this is because when people leave their hometowns for distant lands, their longing and nostalgia grow even stronger.

One’s hometown is the place where one was born and raised. It is a land filled with memories of joys and sorrows shared with parents and family, as well as with neighbors, friends, and schoolmates. It is also a place overflowing with deep emotional ties.

In my hometown, Mount Tsukuba stands majestically amid a vast plain. In every direction around the mountain, gently sloping plains stretch into the distance. At 877 meters, Mount Tsukuba is the only prominent height rising above the plain to the north, forming a range of rugged peaks. That is why whenever I draw a picture, the composition inevitably includes Mount Tsukuba, the nearby river, and the surrounding fields.

I left my hometown in my twenties, and because I also lived abroad for a long time, I was separated from it for many years. Although I returned to visit my parents about once a year, I had become completely distant from my old friends and gradually lost touch with them.

Recently, I returned to Japan and transferred to a new workplace. At that company, I happened to meet someone from my hometown. The mere fact that we came from the same place made the person’s local accent sound incredibly familiar, and we naturally became close.

Salmon, for example, lay their eggs in the upper reaches of a river, and the young fish grow by eating the bodies of their parents. Before long, they travel downstream and begin their journey toward the vast open sea. Yet once they mature, salmon return to the very headwaters of that river to lay their eggs and preserve their species. Then they meet the final moment of their lives in that same place.

For human beings, one’s hometown may also be a place much like that.

(Note 1) 遠くにありて: from a distant place

(Note 2) 詠む: to compose poetry

(Note 3) 室生犀星 (1889–1962): lyric poet and novelist

(Note 4) 募る: to become increasingly intense

(Note 5) 交じり合う: to mix together

(Note 6) 筑波山: a mountain in southwestern Ibaraki Prefecture, one of Japan’s 100 famous mountains

(Note 7) そびえる: to tower majestically, as a mountain or building does

(Note 8) 後にする: to leave behind

(Note 9) 縁遠い: to become distant in one’s relationships with others

(Note 10) 訛り: a local accent or intonation different from standard Japanese

(Note 11) 稚魚: a young fish newly hatched from an egg

(Note 12) 死骸: the dead body of a living creature

(Note 13) 大海原: the vast open sea

(Note 14) 最期を迎える: to meet one’s final moment, to die

default.p.test-19-p1.vietnamese:
In May 2003, the Hayabusa space probe was launched toward the asteroid Itokawa. By September 2005, it had reached Itokawa, and in November of the same year it collected microscopic particles. The probe was then scheduled to return to Earth, but a series of problems, including engine failures, occurred and communication with Earth was lost. As a result, its safe return was once considered almost impossible.

However, in June 2010, Hayabusa, which had been out of contact for so long, approached Earth and landed safely in the Australian desert. The probe overcame problems such as engine failures on its own and spent many years making the long journey back to Earth.

The results of research on the collected microscopic particles were announced. Based on them, researchers discovered that the asteroid Itokawa had formed when an asteroid approximately 20 kilometers in diameter broke apart and the fragments later gathered together again. The microscopic particles remain on Itokawa's surface for no more than about 8 million years and have gradually scattered into outer space. Itokawa, which is peanut-shaped and approximately 500 meters at its longest point, is thought highly likely to disappear completely within the next billion years.

Even so, Hayabusa's safe return gave many people tremendous courage and inspiration. A person in charge at JAXA is holding lectures entitled “The Hayabusa Miracle: Challenge and Revival, Willpower and Perseverance.” The same is true of us: once we undertake a challenge, we must never give up, even if failure is possible. There will certainly be a time when we can rise again and make a fresh start. Until then, patience and determination are absolutely essential.

(Note 1) Planet: a celestial body that orbits the Sun

(Note 2) Microscopic particle: an extremely small, fine particle of matter

(Note 3) Break apart: to split into tiny fragments

(Note 4) JAXA: the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency

(Note 5) Willpower: the determination to pursue something to the very end at any cost

default.p.test-20-p1.vietnamese:
Everyone knows that cigarettes are harmful to one's health. Former U.S. President Bill Clinton is famous for firmly declaring, “Cigarettes are drugs!” Why would someone like him say, “They are drugs!”? As president of a country, did he understand all the harmful effects of cigarettes and say this out of concern for the health of the people? Recently, some people seem to argue that there should also be “smoking areas” for smokers, but to be honest, I just want to call them idiots. Making it easier to smoke cigarettes, which are called a type of drug, is an absurd idea. Some people say that this would be “better” than cigarette butts being thrown around carelessly, but what is bad remains bad. Before proposing smoking areas, why not get rid of the troublesome cigarettes themselves? I am not saying this simply because I do not smoke. It is precisely because smoking causes trouble for others that I want to ask people to give it up.

Some people like ramen, while others like gyudon. Some people love soccer, while others love baseball. The four-character idiom “ten people, ten preferences” means that it is natural for people's tastes and preferences to differ. However, is it really right to judge whether things are right or wrong, good or bad, according to our own likes and dislikes? When nonsmokers chew gum and make smacking or popping sounds, isn't that also a kind of noise? If people have the freedom to make popping sounds while chewing gum, then surely they should also have the right to puff on cigarettes and blow out smoke. I am not unaware of the harm caused by cigarettes, but the idea of calling for “living together” while at the same time saying “that is too bothersome” is fundamentally mistaken. It is precisely because the importance of “living together” matters that someone like me, who does not smoke, says this. Although having many smokers would certainly be bothersome, I think we have to accept creating designated spaces where people can smoke in crowded places.

（Note 1）弊害: Harmful effects; something bad or damaging

（Note 2）知り尽くす: To know completely; to know thoroughly

（Note 3）吸殻: The remaining end of a cigarette after it has been smoked and discarded

（Note 4）唱える: To advocate; to propose

（Note 1）牛丼: Gyudon, a bowl of rice topped with beef

（Note 2）嗜好: Tastes and preferences

（Note 3）物差し: A yardstick; a standard for evaluation

default.p.test-21-p1.outline.0.label: Introduction: The economy in the global-scale era
default.p.test-21-p1.outline.0.note: Introduces the custom of using yen domestically and raises the issue that today's economy has entered an era requiring people to think on a global scale.
default.p.test-21-p1.outline.1.label: Two examples illustrating economic interconnectedness: a shipyard and grape growing.
default.p.test-21-p1.outline.1.note: Example 1: shipbuilding receives an international warning because of oversupply, providing the basis for Question 1. Example 2: grape growing illustrates the law of supply and demand beyond individual control.
default.p.test-21-p1.outline.2.label: The concept of “global” and the necessity of global thinking.
default.p.test-21-p1.outline.2.note: Defines the term 'global' and warns that without global thinking, both businesses and individuals can easily suffer losses (contributes to answering question 3).
default.p.test-21-p1.outline.3.label: The impact of exchange rates on individuals and businesses
default.p.test-21-p1.outline.3.note: Compares using money domestically with exchanging foreign currency, explaining the difference in impact on individuals versus commercial businesses (evidence for question 2).
default.p.test-21-p1.outline.4.label: Conclusion: global monetary thinking and the use of foreign-currency accounts

default.p.test-21-p1.vietnamese:
Normally, we spend money casually without paying much attention to it. To be more precise, because we are Japanese living in Japan, we normally spend yen. Earning yen and then spending yen is perfectly ordinary.

Some people may say, “How could that possibly become a subject for discussion?” Leaving aside the distant past, the economy has somehow entered an age in which it must be considered on a global scale.

For example, suppose a company in Japan is planning to build a shipyard to manufacture ships. Even if it intends to use its own money and build the shipyard itself, it may receive warnings from other companies: “There is currently an oversupply of ships worldwide. Therefore, please reconsider ①what your company plans to do.” Sometimes, warning documents with a complaining tone are also sent by companies in the same industry, both domestic and overseas.

Let us give another example. Suppose people develop a variety of sweet, delicious grapes in order to produce even better fruit. Because the grapes are sweet and delicious, they can be sold at a fairly high price. The farmers who grow them will naturally earn a substantial income and become wealthy.

Once word spreads, farmers throughout the country will rush to grow the grapes, each determined not to be outdone by the others. When that happens, will the grapes still command as high a price as they did at first? Certainly not.

The meaning of “the economy” is also gradually changing with the times. The world has become too small for us to think only about the economy of a single country. The word “global” means “on the scale of the Earth.” We live in an age in which both companies and individuals can easily suffer losses unless they adopt a global way of thinking.

As long as the money earned after a full month of work is used domestically, its value does not change very much. Apart from special items such as gasoline, prices do not fluctuate particularly violently either. However, when one decides to travel abroad and exchange that money for foreign currency, the situation is completely different. ②For individuals, the amount is presumably small, so the impact is limited, but companies engaged in large-scale international transactions absolutely cannot treat such sums lightly.

The yen is indeed Japan's currency. However, if we understand that its value is not always ثابت, exchanging it for dollars when the exchange rate is favorable can produce a small profit.

We live in an age in which even individuals can manage their finances and earn modest profits by making clever use of a stronger or weaker yen. In other words, viewed from the opposite direction, this means that it is “not acceptable” to stop seeing money from a global perspective. Many people may not know this, but banks also offer foreign-currency deposit services that allow customers to deposit and withdraw money directly in foreign currencies. In the coming age, in addition to an ordinary account, it may be advisable to have a global account of this kind.

（Note 1）Warning: Strong advice or a strong request that one wants the other party to follow

（Note 2）Tsukimashite wa: Therefore, for that reason

（Note 3）Fuhei-jimita: Having a dissatisfied, complaining tone

（Note 4）Uruou: To become wealthy; for one's income to increase

（Note 5）Ware saki ni: Competing with determination not to be outdone by others

（Note 6）Fumaete: Taking into consideration; examining

（Note 7）Ura o kaeseba: If considered from the opposite perspective

default.p.test-22-p1.vietnamese:
Mr. Yokoyama, an employee of an automobile-parts company in Tokyo, has recently been suffering from an unexplained toothache. This morning (Monday), while passing in front of a dental clinic, he wrote down the clinic's hours and took the note with him. On Wednesday morning, Mr. Yokoyama has to supervise production at the worksite all morning. He has a lunch appointment with a client at noon. He must go on a business trip from the afternoon and will not return to the company until Thursday afternoon. On Saturday, he plans to go to Shikoku for a relative's wedding. Nakamura Dental Clinic operates by appointment only, and patients cannot be seen unless they make an appointment at least two days in advance. This Friday, the dentist will be busy giving a presentation at an academic conference, so the clinic will be closed all day.

Mr. Yokoyama's business trip was postponed because of arrangements by the partner company and rescheduled for the following Monday. He called to cancel his old appointment and was given a new appointment date.

When carrying out a task, how would you answer if asked whether the result or the process is more important? Depending on the person and the nature of the work, some people would choose the former (the result), while others would value the latter (the process). Therefore, we cannot categorically say, "This is the correct answer." However, from the perspective of someone who has lived for 60 years and spent two-thirds of that time working for a company, I feel that focusing on the process rather than the result tends to lead to better results in the end.

（Note 1）重きを置く: to regard as important

Thanks to advances in medicine, human life expectancy is increasing markedly. Who wouldn’t be interested in living a long life? 「Koki」means「rare since ancient times」and refers to the age of 70. default.p.test-25-p1.vietnamese:
Although people’s bodies differ from one another, a doctor who is my colleague insists that aging begins in the latter half of one’s teens (approximately ages 15–19). Although there are differences depending on eating habits, how one uses the body (physical activity), genetic factors, and so on, this apparently is certain. There are terms such as middle age, adulthood, and old age, but when growth stops in the latter half of the teens, aging begins to catch up with us. If that is true, preparing for old age is not something to begin in one’s 50s or 60s; should we not start around the age of the coming-of-age ceremony (20) instead?

（Note 1）Friends / colleagues: friends. Here, it refers to “a colleague who is a doctor.”

Recently, I have come to think that one of the most serious illnesses of modern times may be computer addiction. default.p.test-28-p1.outline.0.label: Francis Bacon's famous quotation about money
default.p.test-28-p1.outline.0.note: The article opens with a famous quotation by philosopher Francis Bacon about money’s two sides: it is a good servant but a bad master.
default.p.test-28-p1.outline.1.label: The positive side: money is a good servant
default.p.test-28-p1.outline.1.note: Analyzes in detail how money is a good servant: it satisfies daily needs, supports education, enables people to establish schools and companies, and allows them to contribute to the community. Question 1 is based here.
default.p.test-28-p1.outline.2.label: The negative side: Money is a poor master
default.p.test-28-p1.outline.2.note: The discussion shifts to the idea that “money is a bad master”: when people are controlled by money, they may disregard ethics and the law and commit crimes. Question 2 is based on this passage.
default.p.test-28-p1.outline.3.label: The author's conclusion and message
default.p.test-28-p1.outline.3.note: The passage's central message: money is good or bad depending on how it is used; people must understand it in order to control it and avoid letting it become a bad master that causes unhappiness. Question 3 is based on this passage.

default.p.test-28-p1.vietnamese:
「Money is a good servant but a bad master」is a saying by the English philosopher Francis Bacon. I tried reflecting on what this saying means.

First, let us consider point ①「Money is a good servant」. If we have money, we can eat delicious food and wear the fashionable clothes we like. We can also live in a home that suits our tastes, in a place of our choosing. Naturally, we can travel to wonderful destinations. In addition, we can study whatever we want at a university or graduate school, and it is entirely possible to establish a company or a school.

Of course, by donating money to people in need or to society, we can also gain a sense of achievement and satisfaction. In fact, people such as Bill Gates have returned enormous sums of money to society, contributing to cancer research and many other fields of research.

Here, I would like to consider the other side: ②「Money is a bad master」.

First is the idea of treating money as an absolute god. Some people casually do things that go against morality or the law for money. Theft, fraud, prostitution, and ultimately even murder committed to obtain insurance money. Such things seem to be reported in the news every day.

Thus, depending on the circumstances, money can become either a good servant or a bad master. We must understand this deeply and keep it firmly in mind so that we do not submit to an evil master that leads people into unhappiness.

（Note 1）Servant: A person hired in another person’s home to do laundry, cleaning, and other household chores

（Note 2）Return: To restore something to its original state; to give back

（Note 3）Ultimately: In the end; finally

（Note 4）Serve: To serve devotedly; to devote one’s effort and energy to someone

（Note 5）Keep in mind: To pay attention to; to remain cautious

default.p.test-29-p1.vietnamese:
A new type of education, focused on junior and senior high school students and aimed at developing character and personal qualities, is becoming increasingly widespread.

This education began with ideas inspired by education abroad and is based on the world’s best-selling book 「The 7 Habits」. The book was written by American educator Stephen R. Covey. It explains the importance of character qualities such as proactivity, integrity, and cooperation, and is a classic business book that many companies have incorporated into their training programs.

Based on this content, juku schools offering education programs for children and teaching「The 7 Habits」have reached 214 locations nationwide. The program is also spreading to private junior and senior high schools, with about 87 schools currently adopting it across the country.

In this educational program, children learn practically about self-esteem, how to set goals and make plans, and attitudes that earn the trust of others. An eighth-grade student said: 「I learned that I can choose my feelings and reactions, and I am certain that a new me has been born inside me.」When they encounter difficulties in relationships or their studies, they recall those lessons and use them to deal with the situation. This is truly remarkable.

Schools can teach only academic subjects, while parents are busy with work. Junior and senior high school students are also caught up in studying for entrance examinations, so they have very few opportunities to receive education about character or sound ways of thinking. This program is attracting high expectations as something that will make a major contribution to developing children’s character and personal qualities.

（Note 1）Cooperation: The quality of being inclined to make mutual concessions in order to maintain harmony when interests conflict or personalities and opinions differ.

（Note 2）Theory (explanation): An explanation; presenting or stating something.

（Note 3）Juku: A privately established school that provides education for students.

default.p.test-3-p1.vietnamese:
At some point, countless new words related to computers, the Internet, and the economy began to increase—that is, new vocabulary has been appearing in enormous numbers. The creation of new words means that new concepts and knowledge corresponding to them have also emerged.

I myself have just turned 50 and have become so unsure whether I can keep up with the times. Until I graduated from university, I crammed an enormous amount of knowledge into my head, and even after entering the working world, all I did was cram more in. I absolutely hate being an analog, traditional person forced to live in a digital world. No, in one respect, I hate this digital world even more!

(Note 1) Cram (詰め込む): to force oneself to memorize something.

default.p.test-30-p1.vietnamese:
People say that Ameyoko is the heart of the shitamachi, or old downtown district. Ameyoko, short for Ameya Yokocho, has about 400 shops packed along a street approximately 400 meters long.

The area was established not long after the war. At that time, more than 200 shops sold candy, which is why the area came to have this name. Later, jewelry and electronic goods brought in by American soldiers stationed in Japan began to be sold there, and another name, Amerika Yokocho, or America Alley, apparently originated from this. Today, the area is commonly called Ameyoko for both of these reasons.

Ameyoko is unquestionably an ideal place for shopping, and every year at the end of December, the shopping scene there is featured on television.

Because of my work, I often visit Ameyoko, and it is always crowded with people coming and going. Prices can also be reduced by the sellers depending on the negotiation. In particular, if you visit in the late afternoon, fresh seafood may be discounted by as much as half. Located between Ueno Station and Okachimachi Station on the JR Line, it is conveniently accessible, and on occasions such as weekends, the vendors' loud sales calls echo throughout the area.

Recently, foreigners have also opened shops, including Turkish restaurants. Ameyoko is known for its low prices, and it is quite possible to buy famous foreign-brand goods at discounts of 20–30%.

It is also close to Asakusa, a famous tourist destination, and because it attracts many foreign tourists, it has a strongly international atmosphere. When you visit in person and try shopping there, you can truly feel that it is the heart of the old downtown district.

（Note 1）Shitamachi: An urban area near the sea or a river, where many people engaged in commerce and handicrafts live and work.

（Note 2）Yokocho: A narrow alley branching off from a main street.

（Note 3）Spot: A place or location.

（Note 4）Shigotogara: Because of the particular nature of one's work.

（Note 5）Uriko: A person whose job is to sell goods to customers.

（Note 6）Kamaeru: To open a shop.

（Note 7）Masashiku: Truly, certainly.

default.p.test-31-p1.vietnamese:
A
I have heard that a book whose message is "Skipping breakfast will make your body healthier" has become a bestseller, and I am someone who has personally experienced its effects. A few years ago, my symptoms of indigestion and heaviness in the stomach became severe, so I began treating myself by skipping breakfast. I do not know whether this method was truly effective, although I believe it was, but my bloating completely disappeared. I have not actually picked up the book and read it yet, but as someone who has experienced this personally, I would very much like to read it. However, since eating three meals a day is considered perfectly normal in every country and culture, I still wonder whether skipping breakfast is really harmless. Even so, the body is always honest, and the fact that I became healthier is undeniable, so I sympathize with the book's position.

B
I have heard that a book advocating "Skipping breakfast will make your body healthier" has become very popular and is the subject of much discussion, but I think this is a dangerous idea. At night, people fall asleep and rest. However, calories continue to be consumed even while we are resting, so we feel hungry when morning comes. That is why we eat breakfast.

If we do not eat breakfast, energy will not be distributed sufficiently throughout the body, affecting our performance and results at work and school. In fact, statistical findings have shown a significant difference in academic achievement between students who eat breakfast and those who skip it. If eating late at night or being drunk causes indigestion the next morning, there is no need to force oneself to eat. Basically, however, we should not skip breakfast.

(Note 1) 盛り込む (to include): To publish or write something into a text.

(Note 2) 胃もたれ (heaviness in the stomach): A symptom of poor digestion, in which the stomach feels heavy.

(Note 3) 自家療法 (self-treatment): A treatment method based on one's own judgment rather than medical evidence.

(Note 4) 身に覚えがある (to have experienced something personally): To have a memory of experiencing something. Here, it means having personally experienced stomach heaviness that later disappeared.

(Note 1) 眠りにつく (to fall asleep): To go to sleep.

default.p.test-32-p1.outline.1.note: In general, women in every country live longer than men, illustrated by the fact that one sees more elderly women walking bent over than elderly men. Question 1 asks about the evidence represented by “even that one example” (その一つ).
default.p.test-32-p1.outline.2.label: Why men experience more stress and have shorter lifespans
default.p.test-32-p1.outline.2.note: Analyzes the social division of labor: men are expected to go out and earn a living, facing intense competitive pressure that shortens their lives; Question 2 asks about the traditional role (その本来的な姿).
default.p.test-32-p1.outline.3.label: Two ways to reduce stress and extend life expectancy
default.p.test-32-p1.outline.3.note: The author proposes two solutions: (1) do not create stress over whether one's sports team wins or loses (the basis for question 3), and (2) invest time and money in hobbies to relieve stress.
default.p.test-32-p1.outline.4.label: Vocabulary notes in the passage
default.p.test-32-p1.outline.4.note: Definitions of vocabulary and idioms annotated at the end of the reading
default.p.test-32-p1.vietnamese:
People say that whether a person is born male or female is determined by their sex chromosomes. We cannot choose or wish to be born male or female. Whether male or female, the fact remains that we are human beings. Once we are human, surely no one lacks the hope of living a long life.

Without relying on specialized medical knowledge, women generally live longer than men, regardless of country or ethnicity. We often see elderly women bent over with age, whereas the reverse is rarely seen. Even this single example is enough to suggest that women make up the majority of people who live long lives.

As for why this is so, men generally face considerable stress while going out into society to earn a living. Experiments on animals have clearly demonstrated that such stress can shorten life expectancy.

Women, by contrast, use the food and money brought home by men to prepare meals for the family, do the laundry, and are primarily entrusted with raising the children. It is undeniable that we have long since entered an era in which both spouses work to earn money. Nevertheless, whether in terms of the quantity or quality of the means of earning a living, we cannot deny that its basic traditional form has not yet been completely dismantled.

Until they secure a livelihood outside the home, men are often forced, willingly or not, to compete with complete strangers. Naturally, they are highly susceptible to stress. Women, on the other hand, spend most of their daily lives within the family. Even when friction or conflict occurs, it is between family members, so the stress they endure is presumably relatively lighter.

People also say that men are more exposed than women to environments where illness, injury, and accidents are likely to occur, which is another factor shortening average life expectancy. Even so, the greatest cause is surely stress.

This naturally leads us to ask whether there is any effective way to live a long life, and I would like to suggest the following two things.

First, try not to feel too much stress every day. Worrying about whether the team you support will win or lose is simply creating additional stress for yourself. Instead, I think it is better just to enjoy the game itself.

Second, have a hobby that can help reduce stress. That said, hobbies require time and money, so some people may argue that they could become a new source of stress.

However, I would ask in return: if you do not invest at least that much, how can you relieve stress? If you look carefully, you will certainly find activities that require little time or money. Survey results show a real difference in average life expectancy between people who have something interesting they can become absorbed in and those who do not. This has demonstrated the fact clearly and convincingly, more than anything else.

(Note 1) Livelihood: Food or money

(Note 2) Shorten: To become shorter

(Note 3) Cannot deny: Cannot reject as untrue

(Note 4) Willingly or not: Whether one wants to or not

(Note 5) Truthfully: In accordance with the truth, exactly as it is in reality

My grandfather died about 10 years ago. Since he was 98, he had lived almost an entire century. In his final years, only his memory had declined slightly; there were no particular problems with his eyesight or hearing. From time to time, he would call me, his grandchild, over to tell me many stories from the past. What he lectured me about so often that I grew tired of hearing it was waste. He always emphasized that if people lived according to nature's cycle, no waste would be produced. I have now worked at a waste-processing plant for 30 years. As I grow older, I miss him more and more.

（Note 1） Emphasize: to strongly assert or highlight

default.p.test-35-p1.vietnamese:
Although we are definitely twin brothers, my older brother and I have completely opposite personalities. Unlike my quiet older brother, who enjoys music, reading poetry, and painting, I am energetic and spend my time playing outdoor sports such as soccer and baseball until it gets dark. People around me often say things like: 「You’re twins, but your personalities are really different, aren’t they?」 and 「Is it all right for twins to be this different?」. However, from my point of view, this merely proves that they do not understand the difference between outward appearance and inner nature. It is just like boiled eggs and raw eggs: although they look the same on the outside, they are completely different inside.

(Note 1) Aniki: Has the same meaning as “ani” (older brother), but carries a slightly more familiar and intimate nuance.

default.p.test-36-p1.vietnamese:
I hear that a book titled “How to Shop” has become a bestseller. According to the book, expensive goods are not only attractive in appearance but also durable, whereas cheap goods have designs that go without saying (they are very unattractive) and also have short lifespans. The book argues that even if something is a little expensive, it is still “better” than having to buy cheap goods repeatedly. The issue is whether to view things in the long term or think only about immediate benefits.

Of course, if you have plenty of money, there is nothing to worry about. In any case, the book concludes that we should not be deceived by cheap goods whose attractive appearance takes advantage of the superiority of expensive goods.

（Note 1）言うに及ばず: needless to say, it goes without saying

（Note 2）安物: an inexpensive item

default.p.test-37-p1.vietnamese:
With the rapid development of computers and the internet, we are living in a state of information overload unlike anything people have experienced before. If we cannot use computers and the internet skillfully, it will not only be inconvenient but may even cause us to miss many opportunities. I still vividly remember my student days, when I had to rush to the library early in the morning just to look up a few materials. That said, problems such as the reliability of information, its quality, and how to select the information we need are also increasing day by day. Although life seems to be becoming more convenient, we are certainly entering an age full of headaches.

（Note 1）Overflow: Having so much of something that it spills over

（Note 2）A vivid memory: Something that has not been forgotten and is still remembered clearly

（Note 3）Good and bad: What is good and what is not good

The number of different kinds of “cards” is increasing to the point that when someone says “card,” you may not know what they mean. There are Christmas cards, name tags, ATM cards, loyalty cards, memory cards, and many others. The materials used for cards have also changed completely, from paper to plastic and then to cards with embedded chips.

A word formed by adding another word to an existing word is called a compound word. Compound words reflect the development and increasing complexity of society. For example, this can be seen in the change from “road” to “expressway.” Since saying the entire term is cumbersome, people often shorten it, but this can lead to misunderstandings like the one in the example above.

（Note 1）様変わり: a complete change in condition or appearance

default.p.test-39-p1.vietnamese:
「Thrive after every fall」means regaining one's composure, standing up, and continuing to make an effort no matter how many times one stumbles, like the symbolic Daruma doll. It is a saying many people have heard, but quite a few people have actually lived their lives in this way. One thing they often have in common is unhappy childhood memories. When they were young, they experienced both emotional and economic hardship, such as losing their parents, being bullied by friends, or losing their health.

Yet those very experiences of adversity became a「springboard」, fostering an eager desire to rise above their circumstances and a strong spirit of challenge. As a result, they became the foundation for their later success and growth.

By contrast, people who have lived smooth, trouble-free lives and are suddenly thrust into severe adversity can be surprisingly weak and prone to collapse.

On the other hand, some people harbor resentment toward the circumstances of their childhood, become outsiders in society, commit crimes, or enter the underworld.

Those who walk through life with an unwavering spirit of rising after every fall almost certainly have someone who has helped them. When they truly reach an impasse, many of them receive both tangible and intangible assistance that helps them overcome it. Outsiders may simply call this luck, but perhaps invisible help from heaven has come into play. In fact, there is often a deeply devout mother behind them. I cannot help thinking that the mother's heartfelt prayers for her child reached all the way to heaven.

（Note 1）Daruma: A decorative object shaped like Bodhidharma seated in meditation.

（Note 2）Furuitatte: Summoning one's courage and rising with renewed bravery and spirit.

（Note 3）Sono gotoku no jinsei o ayumu: To live a life like that.

（Note 4）Ijime: Bullying or tormenting someone who is weaker or more vulnerable.

（Note 5）Bane: A spring. Here, it means a「chance or turning point that provides motivation」.

（Note 6）Jumpuu mampan: Extremely favorable, with everything proceeding smoothly.

（Note 7）Kukyou: A state of extreme difficulty or hardship.

（Note 8）Moroi: Fragile and easily defeated or broken.

（Note 9）Urami: The desire to retaliate for something someone has done to you; resentment.

（Note 10）Shinjimbukai: Having strong religious faith; deeply devout.

default.p.test-40-p1.outline.0.label: The aging population in Japan
default.p.test-40-p1.outline.0.note: The passage raises the issue of rapidly increasing population aging, with people over 65 accounting for nearly 28%, because advances in medicine have extended life expectancy. This supports question 1.
default.p.test-40-p1.outline.1.label: Average life expectancy exceeding 70 and the paradox of retirement age.
default.p.test-40-p1.outline.1.note: With life expectancy exceeding 80, the term 'Koki' (age 70) is no longer necessary; however, the retirement age has not increased accordingly. Evidence for Question 2.
default.p.test-40-p1.outline.2.label: The nature of aging as a decline in work capacity
default.p.test-40-p1.outline.2.note: Because human physical capacity does not change, actual working time cannot increase; after age 65–70, labor capacity declines. The essence of population aging is an increase in the proportion of people with reduced working capacity.
default.p.test-40-p1.outline.3.label: The dual concern of population aging and the declining birth rate
default.p.test-40-p1.outline.3.note: As the elderly population grows and fewer children are born, Japan’s economic vitality declines, pushing the country toward an uncertain future. This is the main basis for Question 3.
default.p.test-40-p1.outline.4.label: The vocabulary notes in the reading passage
default.p.test-40-p1.outline.4.note: Explanations of vocabulary and special expressions in the passage: Koki (age 70), 稀な, さほど, and 一概には言えない.
default.p.test-40-p1.vietnamese:
One of the problems Japan faces today is its aging population. Population aging is progressing, and people aged 65 and over—also known as the elderly—account for nearly 28% of the population. Thanks to remarkable advances in medical technology 20 to 30 years ago, average life expectancy has increased considerably, and as a result this phenomenon has become increasingly serious.

Long ago, people referred to「Koki」and considered reaching the age of 70 extremely rare, but today, with the average life expectancy of both men and women exceeding 80, it can be said that the term「Koki」is no longer necessary.

Once born as human beings, everyone wishes to live a happy and long life. I do think that a longer life expectancy is a good thing, but we rarely hear of the official retirement age being extended accordingly.

Depending on how one views it, this may be evidence that there is not actually a great difference in people’s innate physical strength between the past and the present. Although average life expectancy has increased because of the rapid development of medical technology, the period during which people can actually work has not increased correspondingly.

Some people run their own businesses and therefore cannot be treated as a group, but as a general assumption, once people are over 65 or 70, it is certainly reasonable to regard their labor capacity as having declined considerably.

Simply put, the true meaning of the phenomenon「population aging」is that the number of people whose ability to work has declined is increasing.

At the same time as population aging, the phenomenon of a「declining birth rate」caused by people having fewer children is also a major problem. The growing number of elderly people is already a serious issue, and the fact that new lives are no longer being born is another significant cause for concern. When children are no longer born, the economy and industry tend to lose vitality, and the impact is enormous.

Today, Japan continues to grapple with the problems of an aging society and a declining-birthrate society, like a ship drifting at sea with no future in sight.

（Note 1）Koki: A term expressing age. It means 70 years old.

（Note 2）Rare: Uncommon / hardly ever seen

（Note 3）さほど: To that extent

（Note 4）Cannot be generalized: It is not necessarily the same in every case.

default.p.test-41-p1.vietnamese:
As environmental problems become increasingly serious, Japan’s automobile market is showing a shift in demand from conventional gasoline- and diesel-powered cars to hybrid and electric vehicles. However, this trend is strong only in Japan; in Europe, particularly Germany, diesel cars remain very popular.

The reasons diesel cars are disliked in Japan include the large amount of soot they emit and their noisy engines. Along with Tokyo’s「No Diesel Vehicle Campaign」, launched in Heisei 11 (1999), and the world’s strictest emissions regulations, implemented in Heisei 9 (1997), opposition to diesel cars grew increasingly strong.

However, it is surprising that in Europe, particularly Germany, as many as 50% of cars are diesel-powered. In addition to their inherently excellent fuel efficiency, technological innovation has reduced soot and noise, and models that meet the world’s strictest emissions regulations have appeared. Diesel cars are said to have superior acceleration and stability, and to be easy to handle skillfully, making driving enjoyable. Moreover, their fuel economy is 20 to 30% better than that of gasoline-powered cars, which is another reason they are popular.

In contrast to Europe, which is highly sensitive and strict about environmental pollution, Japan is becoming increasingly interested in hybrid and electric vehicles. However, in the future, after considering their characteristics, perhaps we should also include clean, high-performance diesel-engine vehicles among our options when buying a car.

（Note 1）依然として: still, continuing to be the same up to the present

（Note 2）すす: black powder contained in smoke or flames (soot)

（Note 3）逆風: opposition, an anti-diesel movement

（Note 4）持ち前: inherent, naturally possessed

（Note 5）クリアする: to meet or exceed a standard

default.p.test-42-p1.vietnamese:
A
When a company posts a job advertisement, setting limits on gender or age is based on each company’s particular circumstances and is not intended to restrict anyone. For example, for dangerous work such as climbing utility poles, would it not be impossible to hire elderly people or women? If the main job is customer service, can one really say that older men must be hired? Companies, organizations, and groups all have goals and policies they pursue, and they have the right to hire people suited to the work they assign. It is difficult when outsiders simplistically label this as gender or age discrimination. Of course, some jobs have nothing to do with gender, and there are cases where being slightly older does not prevent someone from doing the work. However, as the saying “the right person for the right job” indicates, every job has people who are and are not suited to it, so it is intolerable for outsiders to discuss and judge a company’s right to choose its employees.

B
I acknowledge that some people are more or less suited to particular jobs. I can also understand a company’s individual preferences when hiring. However, what I want to point out here is the irrationality of deciding in advance who will be hired or what age group will be recruited. A difference of only one year does not cause a clear decline in physical strength, and it is unreasonable to hastily conclude that a woman will probably have difficulty doing the job. Judging people’s abilities by numbers or based on gender differences is utterly absurd. Take interpreting, for example: experience plays a much greater role than age or physical strength. Yet I genuinely wonder what basis people have for arbitrarily setting limits according to age or gender. I only hope people will not make the foolish mistake of hastily judging a person’s abilities by gender and age.

(Note 1) Elderly person: An old person or someone approaching old age.

(Note 2) Suitability: A situation in which something is suitable or unsuitable.

(Note 3) Intolerable: Difficult to endure or put up with.

(Note 1) To demonstrate effectiveness: To show one’s effect or effectiveness.

(Note 2) Hasty judgment: Reaching a conclusion hastily without fully checking the facts.

default.p.test-43-p1.vietnamese:
For human beings, working is a natural part of life. If they were forced to lie in bed all day without doing anything, they surely could not endure the suffering.

For human beings, having time to rest is only natural. If, hypothetically, there were no time to rest and people continued working without sleeping, they too would surely be unable to endure such hardship.

For human beings, learning is essential. Anyone who tries to act without learning is like someone walking through unfamiliar territory without a map; in the end, they will likely repeat failure in everything they do.

For human beings, love is life itself. It is so closely tied to our existence that when people lose love, they may even take their own lives.

That is why people decided to set aside eight hours for work, both as a right and an obligation; eight hours for sleep and rest; and eight hours to live freely, learning and loving.

In the past, sunlight, water, air, and time were distributed equally to everyone. However, capitalist civilization polluted the air, contaminated water sources, and created people who had to live where sunlight could not reach. Time alone, however, is gradually becoming more equally distributed: excessive and unequal working hours in the past have been reduced, while transportation has developed.

Indeed, among some people, there have begun to appear those who feel overwhelmed and do not know how to manage their free time and study time.

Just as a person with money can become a failure in life if they use it poorly, a person with too much free time may also fall behind in life if they use it improperly.

As the proverb says, “Study hard and play hard,” depending on how well we study and how healthily we enjoy our free time, should we not be able to become healthy in both mind and body, work effectively, and develop ourselves into capable people who can forge our own paths in life?

(Note 1) Being forced: being compelled to do something against one’s will

(Note 2) Endure: to bear patiently, to put up with

(Note 3) Entrust/impose: to force someone to take on a responsibility

(Note 4) Overwhelmed and at a loss: having difficulty managing or using something

(Note 5) Mistake: doing something incorrectly, confusing one thing with another

(Note 6) Forge a path: to explore and open the way

default.p.test-45-p1.vietnamese:
There is a saying,「Time is money」, and lately I have been feeling the truth of it more deeply. I have a friend who once opened a shop but failed. At first business went fairly well, but problems arose along the way, and in the end he had to close the shop. His main job now is driving a taxi. Even on his days off, he works part-time at a convenience store. He is filled with determination to repay all his debts and prove that he can recover once again. He laughs wryly and says,「Rather than watching TV when I have free time, I would rather work」and「Songs are nothing more than lullabies」. When one thinks about the limited amount of「time」in a person's life, one cannot simply spend it idly.

（注釈1）nari: to be (affirmative form)

（注釈2）ii sen iku: to do well in business, to prosper

（注釈3）ikigomu: to make every effort, to be determined

Ideally, they should be thoroughly taught about the company's development and how to do their work before being assigned their duties, but small and medium-sized businesses often tend to neglect this. As someone whose job is to help businesses learn ways to improve productivity, I sincerely hope they will not do this. It is not a matter of "ignorance is bliss." Rather, "ignorance means suffering losses." I earnestly hope everyone will remember this.

(Note 1) Ignorance is Buddha: It is better not to know the truth than to know it.

default.p.test-47-p1.vietnamese:
After ranking first in the final examination of the second term in the sixth grade of elementary school, I was continually praised as an excellent student until I graduated from high school. At the time, I hated classes such as physical education, music, and art so much that I still remember those feelings vividly today. I used to think that studying subjects such as English, mathematics, and language arts was all that mattered.

However, just as nutrition must not be unbalanced, I now clearly understand, from the perspective of a well-rounded education, how important the classes I once hated really were. They are indispensable for developing a well-rounded character.

（Note 1）Public praise/commendation: Praising someone's achievements in front of others

（Note 2）Well-rounded education: An overall education that includes not only knowledge and skills but also emotions and morals.

The other day, I went to a movie theater for the first time in a long while. Watching a movie alone is not very enjoyable, but since it was a highly anticipated film, I decided to go even though I was by myself. The theater was packed, but in the darkness I finally found my reserved seat.

The movie began, and a scene appeared on the screen in which the main character was being chased by someone. I watched the subtitles with intense concentration. Perhaps only two or three minutes had passed. The fatigue from work suddenly caught up with me, and I began to feel sleepy. It was at that very moment. The main character and the unidentified person began punching and kicking each other in a furious fistfight. (The rest is omitted.)

(Note 1) たどり着く: to finally reach a place, after having difficulty getting there

(Note 2) 何者: a person whose identity or background is unknown

(Note 3) 殴り合い: a fight in which both sides punch each other

My 38-year-old friend, who graduated from a prestigious business university, is highly proficient with computers and has a keen sense of economics, yet he suffered such heavy losses in the stock market that he had to sell both the land inherited from his ancestors and the condominium where he lived. I hear that he once made quite a lot of money through stocks, but he suffered losses because of the economic downturn and his excessive greed. By contrast, my elderly neighbor, who knows nothing about the Internet, is remarkably good at buying and selling land and houses. He not only raised his children but also sent all three of his grandchildren to study in the United States. Indeed, there are quite a few cases in which the 'wisdom of the elderly' shines far more brightly than the 'knowledge and instincts of the young.'

（注釈1）Hame: a difficult situation, a predicament

（注釈2）Mōkeru: to make a profit, to earn money

default.p.test-50-p1.vietnamese:
I would like to consider the value of things we can see and things we cannot see. The counterpart of the word 'personality' is 'physical form.' Personality probably refers to invisible qualities such as a person's character and virtue, while physical form literally refers to that person's body, such as their muscles and skeleton. When comparing personality and physical form—which correspond to the human mind and body, both of which are necessary—being praised for having an excellent personality generally makes people feel happier.

When considering human health and life, the factors that sustain life include food (nutrients) and air (oxygen). Both are necessary, but without air (oxygen), human life cannot be maintained for even 5 minutes. Indeed, the invisible air is even more important.

There are people in this world who say that they believe only in things they can see. Yet even such people instinctively put their hands together and pray to the gods and Buddha when placed in a situation in which they are powerless to do anything.

In worlds such as professional sports, results are absolute, and everything is evaluated based on those visible results. However, it is truly surprising that, in such an environment, more athletes who have made their names in history speak about the importance of the spiritual side.

People sometimes become so preoccupied with visible things that they lose sight of their essential nature—the invisible world.

(Endnote 1) 持たない: being unable to maintain that state

(Endnote 2) 神仏: gods and Buddha

(Endnote 3) 時として: sometimes

default.p.test-51-p1.vietnamese:
I feel great admiration when I see people who work in the arts, especially music, or students studying at universities for that purpose. First of all, it is wonderful that they can choose something they love as their profession. Art soothes the heart while also bringing vitality, joy, and emotion. Of course, it is also highly effective in relieving stress.

Sports have some similarities, but art brings greater and more direct joy. Hard rock is not particularly to my taste, but I am fascinated by people walking along the street carrying instruments such as violins or cellos.

Music is also very useful in treating illness. When my father fell, hit his head, and was hospitalized with symptoms similar to Alzheimer’s disease, a music therapist sang nostalgic old songs for elderly people to him. The other elderly patients were also delighted and joined in.

On the televised singing competition Nodo Jiman, there was also someone who had once collapsed from a cerebral infarction but recovered through karaoke as a form of rehabilitation and appeared on the program.

I used to sing in a choir, too, and I miss that time very much. If I have the opportunity, I would like to join a choir again. I also feel that I understand why karaoke is so popular among busy office workers.

(Note 1) 和む (nagomu): For one’s mood to become relaxed and relieved.

(Note 2) ハードロック (hard rock): An energetic and powerful genre of rock music.

(Note 3) 携える (tazusaeru): To carry something with oneself.

(Note 4) 心が惹かれる (kokoro ga hikareru): To become interested in something and feel drawn to it.

(Note 5) アルツハイマー病 (Alzheimer’s disease): A brain disorder that causes memory loss.

(Note 6) 懐メロ (natsumero): Old melodies and songs that evoke memories.

(Note 7) のど自慢 (nodo jiman): A singing contest.

(Note 8) 脳梗塞 (cerebral infarction): A disease caused by a blocked blood vessel in the brain.

(Note 9) リハビリ (rehabilitation): A comprehensive therapeutic training process to help people with physical disabilities return to life in society.

default.p.test-52-p1.vietnamese:
How far will the development of science and technology continue? It was about 150 years ago that human beings, who had previously used ox carts and horse-drawn carriages, invented automobiles. Automobiles were invented as a means of transporting people and also for carrying goods. Over time, they have continued to change in appearance and form.

First, their scale has gradually grown larger. A larger scale means that engine power has become stronger. From another perspective, it also means that progress has been made in reducing the weight of vehicles. Vehicles have also become faster. Naturally, riding comfort has improved greatly as well.

At first, there were vehicles that could carry only two or three people. Later, large buses capable of carrying dozens of people were developed, and all kinds of vehicles now travel the roads according to their purposes: commuter cars, cargo vehicles, touring cars, sports cars, construction vehicles, and even vehicles used as homes. Here, what we must never forget is the scale of accidents. An ox cart or horse-drawn carriage might cause only two or three casualties, but a double-decker bus accident could take the lives of dozens of people. The more convenient vehicles become, the more incomparable the price of unexpected consequences becomes compared with the past.

Human greed in the pursuit of convenience has no limit. We have entered the era of so-called “fully autonomous driverless vehicles,” making maximum use of cutting-edge technology. It seems that even self-driving vehicles have different levels of safety. Surely, before long, the highest-level self-driving vehicle—both safe and convenient—will appear.

Although I use my own car, I am an outsider when it comes to automobiles. I have many doubts about how a car can drive itself when there is no driver at all. I hear that advances in sensors have made driverless driving possible, but what would happen if the sensors happened to malfunction?

It is true that science and technology are continually advancing. Surely no one wishes for technology not to develop. However, no matter how innovative the products created in the future may be, what truly matters is creating products that are both safe and do not burden the Earth. In any case, please do not let unsafe things appear and throw society into chaos.

（注1）牛車：in the past, a vehicle for nobles or for transporting goods pulled by oxen

（注2）乗り心地：the feeling of riding in a vehicle

（注3）代償：a price or sacrifice paid in return

（注4）且つ：and at the same time

（注5）門外漢：a person who does not know much about a particular field

（注6）ひとりでに：naturally, by itself

default.p.test-53-p1.vietnamese:
A
Against the backdrop of the rapidly growing demand for English in recent years, our country's foreign-language policy has quite a few problems. There is understandable justification for focusing so much on national-language education, in order to enable future generations to carry on traditional Japanese culture and to learn kanji, which are considered relatively difficult to memorize.

However, even given these circumstances, beginning English education only in junior high school is far too late. Among Asian countries, very few have an average TOEFL score as low as Japan's.

For Japanese people, learning the Japanese language and Japanese culture is only natural. I am not saying that this is a bad thing. However, for Japan, a country poor in natural resources, the only way to survive is through foreign trade. To promote trade, it is essential to acquire the world's international language, English, from an early age. Considering children's flexibility in pronunciation and their ability to expand their access to information, introducing English education widely at an early age is an urgent necessity.

B
The countries and peoples of the world have created their own distinctive cultures together with the natural environments in which they live, and have passed those cultures on to future generations through their own languages and writing systems. Countries with maritime cultures have rich expressions related to fish and seaweed, while places where wet-rice cultivation has flourished have passed down diverse expressions corresponding to that way of life. It cannot be denied that England, an island nation in Europe, increased its national power and expanded throughout the world, and that English has now established itself as a representative world language.

However, human culture has developed on the foundation of diversity, and development lacking diversity is difficult to expect. I do not intend to ignore the power of English as a so-called international language, but even so, it cannot express every aspect of human life and phenomena. The six years of elementary school are an extremely important period for learning one's own country's language and culture. Having English take time away from such an important period is entirely unreasonable.

(Note 1) 昨今: today, in recent years

(Note 2) わが国: our country, Japan

(Note 1) 稲作: rice cultivation

(Note 2) 事象: event, phenomenon

(Note 3) 理に適う: to be reasonable, to accord with reason or principle

default.p.test-54-p1.vietnamese:
I opened a small convenience store exactly one year after my husband went missing. My husband was a mountaineer. He had been innately passionate about climbing since childhood, to the extent that he spent half of every year climbing mountains.

Last March, my husband set out with a mountaineering party determined to conquer Mount Everest in the Himalayas. Exactly one month later, he went missing. When I was informed of the accident, I fainted.

Although I had waited for an entire year, I could not go on waiting forever for a husband who would not return. In order to raise our children, I sold the inheritance he had left behind and opened a small convenience store. I have two children: my older daughter is in first grade at elementary school, while my younger son is still in kindergarten.

① "Mom, Dad is working in America, right? He is coming home soon, right?" Whenever my son was about to forget how much he missed his father, he would say this as if reminding himself not to forget him. This verbal habit developed because I had lied to the children, telling them that their father, who had not returned, was doing work related to mountaineering in America.

At first, my older daughter also seemed to believe me, but recently she appears to have learned the truth. Tears suddenly streamed down my cheeks—I had always told myself that I had to live bravely and never let myself cry—at the moment I heard my daughter say, ② "That's right, Dad is working in America," joining in with her little brother's story.

"If you meet someone you like, you should remarry. These days, families with stepchildren are hardly unusual!" my mother-in-law advised me. But I had never considered divorcing the husband who loved mountains and had married the mountains. Living bravely and raising our children to become fine adults so that he could see them—that is the only love I can give my late husband.

"Please always watch over the children and me. I promise I will raise them well."

It was time to hand over the store to the part-time employee. On my way home, as I looked up at the stars in the night sky, I realized that I had somehow developed the habit of thinking about my husband's smile.

(Note 1) 根っから (nekkara): innately, by nature

(Note 2) 失神 (shisshin): to faint, lose consciousness

(Note 3) 相づちを打つ (aizuchi o utsu): to listen to what the other person says and respond in agreement

(Note 4) ステップファミリー (stepfamily): a remarried family with stepchildren

(Note 5) 義母 (gibo): mother-in-law (the spouse's mother)

(Note 6) 亡き夫 (naki otto): deceased husband

(Note 7) 仰ぐ (aogu): to look up

default.p.test-6-p1.vietnamese:
Some people suffer from diseases affecting organs such as the heart, liver, kidneys, and eyes (retinas), causing their functions to deteriorate and placing their lives in danger. They eagerly await organ donations from people who have been declared brain-dead, but in reality, the number of people hoping for transplants far exceeds the number of donors. As a result, many patients are forced to lose their lives. Furthermore, even when a donated organ is received, the patient's life cannot be saved if the body rejects the organ from another person.

Against this background, news a few years ago that iPS cells (a new type of pluripotent stem cell) could be created by transforming a person's own skin cells into various other types of cells became a major topic of discussion. The common method of creating iPS cells is to introduce four types of genes into cells such as skin cells. One of the four is called C-Myc, a cancer-causing gene, and experiments on mice reportedly resulted in cancer in as many as 70% of cases. Therefore, a university research team replaced C-Myc with a gene called L-Myc, and as a result, the risk of developing cancer apparently disappeared. The efficiency of producing iPS cells also reportedly increased dramatically, which is truly astonishing. Thanks to this, we have moved one step closer to putting regenerative medicine into practice, for example, through organ transplants using iPS cells. Because these cells are created from the patient's own cells, they do not trigger rejection and have outstanding advantages.

I have great hopes for further research and development in the future.

(Note 1) Be placed in danger: be put in a dangerous situation

(Note 2) Lose one's life: die

(Note 3) Production efficiency: the efficiency of manufacturing or producing something

default.p.test-7-p1.vietnamese:
Since the rainy season ended, the intense heat of midsummer has continued for many days in a row. It is hot throughout the country, and temperatures have risen unusually high in some places, reaching 37 or 38 degrees. There have also been cases of people dying from heatstroke. Many people have collapsed while farming or being outdoors, and some have even collapsed inside their homes and had to be taken to emergency hospitals. The situation is truly far from normal.

The cause of this intense heat is the Pacific High, which is said to be stronger than usual this year. The Pacific High forms when heated air rises in the equatorial region, loses its escape route in the upper atmosphere, and then sinks around 30 degrees north latitude southeast of Japan. As this air sinks, it is compressed and becomes hotter. This year, the Pacific High is said to be even stronger because an additional flow of air is descending from air that rose over the waters near the Philippines. It is also believed that the intense heat over the Japanese archipelago has been amplified by the westerlies, which are also responsible for unusual weather phenomena around the world, such as the heat wave in Russia.

In any case, this is thought to be deeply connected with global warming. Countries need to cooperate to reduce CO2 emissions, but because the issue is tied to economic concerns, progress has been slow. Countries around the world, especially developed and developing countries, have been unable to reach agreement. Firm efforts to coordinate their views are needed, but all we can do is pray that it will not become too late.

（Note 1）Tsuyu (rainy season): A period of continuous rain around June

（Note 2）Mōshobi (extremely hot day): A day when the temperature reaches 35 degrees or higher

（Note 3）Netchūshō (heatstroke): A disorder or injury caused by exercising or working in high temperatures

（Note 4）Tadagoto dewa nai (not an ordinary matter): Abnormal, unusual
