default.p.test-8-p1.vietnamese:
If human life is assumed to last 80 years, it is said that after subtracting time spent sleeping, eating and drinking, engaging in economic activity, and being caught up in various daily chores, only about 8 years remain.

Although we are born into this world and live for 80 years, the time we can use purely for ourselves amounts to only 8 years. Calculated per day, it is not even 30 minutes.

For one person, these 8 years may amount to only 1 year, while for another they may become 8 years or even several decades. A person's value will be revealed through the content and quality of those 8 years. When that person dies, how they lived during the time devoted solely to themselves will become the trace they leave for future generations.

During this time reserved solely for themselves, some people do nothing but watch television. Others enjoy books and read passionately, while still others live according to their own interests. Some devote themselves to volunteer or charitable activities, and some earnestly spread their religion, while others remain absorbed in having fun, gambling, and frequenting bars.

People use this time in wonderfully diverse ways, but when I realized that how a person uses their private time determines their value and becomes the judgment of future generations, I was suddenly struck by the realization. This was because I myself had not yet learned how to use my time fully and meaningfully.

The final moment of life will come to everyone, but recently I have kept telling myself that I must use this precious time that belongs only to me meaningfully, so that I will have no regrets when that moment arrives.

(Note 2) 痕跡: traces that reveal what existed in the past

(Note 3) 励む: to make every effort, work diligently

(Note 4) 戯れる: to play around enjoyably, remain absorbed in having fun

(Note 5) ハッとする: to be startled by something unexpected

default.p.test-9-p1.vietnamese:
A
What are some things that people must not do? There are probably many, such as murder, lying, theft, financial fraud, violence, and wastefulness. Of all these, the thing that must absolutely never be done is surely murder. For example, if someone accidentally beat another person to death during a major argument or fight, one might be able to understand it to some extent, although it would still be wrong.

However, no one in the world could sympathize with or understand a crime such as forcibly abducting a woman exhausted from work as she walks home, then assaulting and killing her.

Some people are always complaining about the dignity of human life and similar matters, but the reason why the death penalty must be maintained has become perfectly clear through this murder case. Considering the victim and her family, it is only natural that the death penalty should be maintained.

B
Murder is certainly the thing people must absolutely never do. Moreover, forcibly taking away a passerby who has no connection whatsoever with the perpetrator, dragging that person away for no reason, and then killing them after assaulting them is unforgivable under any circumstances. Even if people say the perpetrator deserves the death penalty, that cannot be helped. However, I think there is a problem with executing someone simply because they have made a serious mistake. This is because there are sometimes cases in which it cannot be established with certainty that the person is actually the perpetrator.

For someone who has committed such a brutal murder, talking about human dignity may seem strange, but what concerns me most is whether we can be 100% certain that this person is truly the culprit. What if the person is not the real culprit? Murder cannot be tolerated, but the death penalty is unacceptable. Even if the person really is the culprit, giving them a chance to atone may be more effective in deterring crime. I want the death penalty to be abolished.

（Note 1）偶発的に: accidentally

（Note 2）強引に: forcibly

（Note 1）道行く: walking along the street

（Note 2）無残な: brutal, merciless

（Note 3）懸念する: to be concerned about, to worry about
default.q.test-22-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) Next Tuesday
The business trip was postponed until the following Monday, while the days of this week were unavailable because of existing schedules or the rule requiring reservations two days in advance. Therefore, the earliest day Mr. Yokoyama can see the doctor is next Tuesday.
default.q.test-22-q1-1.explanation: In terms of the information provided, the basis is the quotation: 「横山さんの出張が相手会社の都合により、延期になり、来週の月曜日に行くことになった。」 (Mr. Yokoyama’s business trip was postponed due to circumstances at the other company and is now scheduled for next Monday). The key grammar pattern is 「V-ることになった」(using the dictionary form), which describes a decision or arrangement determined by external circumstances rather than the subject’s intention. The passage also contains 「２日前までに予約しないと診てもらえない」, which uses the obligatory conditional pattern 「〜ないと...ない」(if A is not done, B cannot happen), requiring an appointment to be made at least two days before the medical examination. A common trap is answer choice (c): learners may skim the final sentence and notice the time reference while overlooking 「延期」(postponed), mistakenly thinking Monday is the examination date rather than the business-trip date. Because Mr. Yokoyama is unavailable next Monday due to the business trip, the earliest date satisfying both his availability and the clinic’s advance-booking rule is the following Tuesday.
default.q.test-22-q1-1.why.0: ✗ (a) The dental clinic requires reservations at least 2 days in advance, so it is too late on Monday morning to book an appointment for Tuesday afternoon.
default.q.test-22-q1-1.why.1: ✗ (b) On Wednesday morning, Mr. Yokoyama is busy supervising production at the worksite and has a lunch appointment with a client.
default.q.test-22-q1-1.why.2: ✗ (c) The business trip was postponed to next Monday, so he cannot go for a medical examination then.
default.q.test-22-q1-1.why.3: ✓ (d) Next Tuesday is the earliest time Mr. Yokoyama is available after his business trip and still early enough to make a reservation as required.
default.q.test-22-q2-2.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (b) 今週の水曜日の午後
The clinic requires an appointment two days in advance, counting from Monday morning, so the earliest possible appointment is Wednesday. In addition, Mr. Yokoyama's business trip originally scheduled for Wednesday afternoon was postponed until next week, making this the earliest time he can visit the clinic.
default.q.test-22-q2-2.explanation: Grammatically, the structure `V-る / V-ない + ことになる`, combined with the plain form, expresses a decision or plan that has changed because of circumstances beyond one's control. It is used with a noun and `〜により` to state the cause formally, as in: 「横山さんの出張が相手会社の都合により、延期になり、来週の月曜日に行くことになった。」 (Mr. Yokoyama's business trip was postponed due to circumstances at the other company, and it was decided that he would go next Monday.) According to the dental clinic's rule, 「２日前までに予約しないと診てもらえない」 (you cannot be seen unless you make an appointment at least two days in advance), and because the information was checked on Monday morning (「けさ（月曜）」), the earliest day the clinic could accept the patient was Wednesday. Although the original schedule said 「午後から出張」 (the business trip would begin in the afternoon), postponing the trip freed Wednesday afternoon as the first available time slot. For schedule questions, always check both the provider's minimum acceptance conditions and the character's actual free time after the information is updated, rather than mistakenly choosing (c) or (d), which are later than the earliest possible time.
default.q.test-22-q2-2.why.0: ✗ (a) This choice is incorrect because Mr. Yokoyama has to be at the production site supervising manufacturing all Wednesday morning and then has a lunch appointment with a business partner.
default.q.test-22-q2-2.why.1: ✓ (b) This choice is correct because the clinic accepts appointments at least 2 days in advance (counting from Monday), and the Wednesday afternoon business trip was postponed until the following week, leaving him free to visit the clinic.
default.q.test-22-q2-2.why.2: ✗ (c) This choice is incorrect because, although Thursday morning is available, Wednesday afternoon is the earliest time at which the appointment can be accepted.
default.q.test-22-q2-2.why.3: ✗ (d) This choice is incorrect because next week is too late compared with the request to find the earliest possible time; moreover, he will be busy on a make-up business trip at the beginning of next week.
default.q.test-34-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) お祖父さんに、いつもかわいがられていた。
By describing how his grandfather often called him aside to tell stories about the past, kindly teach him about life, and became increasingly missed as he grew older, the author emphasizes the deep affection and loving care his grandfather always gave him.
default.q.test-34-q1-1.explanation: To identify the author’s central message, connect the opening reminiscence 「祖父は、ときおり孫の私を呼んで、昔の話をよく聞かせてくれた。」 with the emotional conclusion 「歳を重ねていけばいくほど、お祖父さんが恋しくなる。」. At N2 level, the passage uses the proportional pattern 「V-ば V-ほど」, here in the variant 「V-ていけばいくほど」, with a conditional form and dictionary form to mean “the more..., the more...,” showing how the speaker’s feelings intensify with time and life experience. The conclusion means: “The older I get and the more years of life I go through, the more deeply I miss and long for my grandfather.” This deep nostalgia comes from the speaker’s childhood, when the grandfather lovingly and indulgently told stories, as expressed by the benefactive 「聞かせてくれた」. In N2 reading comprehension, watch for absolute wording such as 「全くなかった」 in choice (b), which contradicts 「記憶力が少し弱くなったくらいで」. Also distinguish the devices that trigger memories, such as the garbage and workplace in (c) and (d), from the author’s actual central idea.
default.q.test-34-q1-1.why.0: ✓ (a) The author’s grandfather called them over to tell stories about the past, reminded them of many things from childhood, and became increasingly missed over the years. This shows that the author was always deeply loved and cherished by their grandfather.
default.q.test-34-q1-1.why.1: ✗ (b) The passage clearly states that the grandfather’s memory had deteriorated slightly in his later years (「記憶力が少し弱くなった」). Therefore, claiming that he had absolutely no health problems (「全くなかった」) is incorrect.
default.q.test-34-q1-1.why.2: ✗ (c) The discussion of waste was merely a topic the grandfather emphasized when teaching the author during his lifetime. The passage does not mention that the waste problem is becoming increasingly serious.
default.q.test-34-q1-1.why.3: ✗ (d) The detail that he worked at a waste-processing plant for 30 years merely provides background that evokes his advice. There is no information indicating that the author gradually felt exhausted or tired.
default.q.test-36-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) 質の落ちる安物を、高い値段で買ったりしないように注意すべきだ。
The book’s final sentence summarizes its central message: consumers should be careful not to be deceived into buying cheap, low-quality products disguised as high-quality goods and sold at high prices.
default.q.test-36-q1-1.explanation: The author’s main message appears in the concluding sentence: 「何はともあれ、高い物のよさを悪用する、形だけの安物にはだまされないように、とその本はしめくくっている。」This means: “In any case, the book concludes by advising readers not to be deceived by cheap goods that merely imitate the appearance of expensive products in order to exploit their good qualities.” The key grammar point is `V-ない + ように（しめくくる）`, which follows the short negative form to convey an indirect reminder or warning: “be careful not to...” The phrase 「高い物のよさを悪用する、形だけの安物」refers to low-quality goods that borrow the name and appearance of expensive products to deceive buyers into paying an exorbitant price. Test takers may be trapped by choice (d) because it contains an idea resembling 「形だけ」, but the key is 「悪用」—the dishonest act of exploiting the valuable qualities of good products to sell something at a high price—which only choice (c) captures accurately.
default.q.test-36-q1-1.why.0: ✗ (a) The author does not recommend recognizing the value of expensive goods even when finances are tight; the author simply states that if one has money, there is no need to worry.
default.q.test-36-q1-1.why.1: ✗ (b) The passage does not discuss valuing quality over price; its main point is avoiding being deceived while shopping.
default.q.test-36-q1-1.why.2: ✓ (c) This choice accurately reflects the book’s conclusion: be wary of paying an inflated price for a low-quality product.
default.q.test-36-q1-1.why.3: ✗ (d) This choice overlooks the intention to exploit the advantages of expensive products (高い物のよさを悪用する) and adds an unsupported conclusion about shopping reasonably.
default.q.test-38-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (b) 高速道路のように
The phrase 「例のように」 directly refers to the example 「高速道路」 given by the author in the preceding sentence to illustrate a compound word.
default.q.test-38-q1-1.explanation: The grammar pattern 「N + のように」 means “like ...” or “as ...,” and is used to introduce a typical example or refer to a specific illustrative object already mentioned. In the passage, the underlined sentence is: 「長くなった言葉を全部言うのは面倒だから、縮めて言うのだが、それが例のように誤解を生じさせるわけである。」, meaning: “Because saying the entire lengthened expression is troublesome, people shorten it, but this causes misunderstandings, as in the example.” Earlier, the author gives the exact example: 「例えば、道路⇒高速道路でも分かるように。」, in which 「高速道路」 is the compound noun illustrating how an expression becomes longer. When answering this type of reading-comprehension question, look immediately at the preceding sentence for the specific noun following 「例えば」. Do not mistakenly choose a general concept such as 「複合語」 or a distant example such as 「カード」.
default.q.test-38-q1-1.why.0: ✗ (a) 「道路」is merely the original base word before developing into a more complex compound, so it is not the example of lengthening being discussed.
default.q.test-38-q1-1.why.1: ✓ (b) 「高速道路」 is the specific compound word given as an illustrative example in the preceding sentence, immediately following the adverb 「例えば」.
default.q.test-38-q1-1.why.2: ✗ (c) 「複合語」 is the general term for a linguistic phenomenon, not a specific example itself.
default.q.test-38-q1-1.why.3: ✗ (d) 「カード」 is discussed in the first paragraph, so it falls outside the direct referential scope of this sentence.
default.q.test-49-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) 主人公がその何者かと殴り合いのけんかを始めた瞬間
The phrase 「その瞬間だった」 is used as a literary device to introduce and emphasize the dramatic event that follows: the moment when the protagonist began fighting with the person who was chasing them.
default.q.test-49-q1-1.explanation: The time noun combined with the past auxiliary verb forms a separate sentence, 「その瞬間だった」, creating a dramatic pause. This narrative device draws the reader’s attention to a sudden event that occurs immediately in the following sentence. The relevant passage is: 「その瞬間だった。主人公がその何者かと、殴り合いのけんかを始めた。」The sentence means: “It was at that very moment that the protagonist began fighting with the unidentified person.” Learners may be tempted to choose (a) because 「その」seems to refer back to the state 「眠くなってきた」in the preceding sentence. In N2 reading comprehension, when a short time expression such as 「その時だった」or「その瞬間だった」appears as a separate sentence, look immediately at the following sentence: it points forward to the imminent event that the author wants to highlight.
default.q.test-49-q1-1.why.0: ✗ (a) The author’s feeling sleepy is merely a background condition that occurred beforehand, not the dramatic event placed in focus.
default.q.test-49-q1-1.why.1: ✗ (b) In the passage, the main character is being chased and fighting; there is no detail about being sleepy.
default.q.test-49-q1-1.why.2: ✓ (c) The phrase 「その瞬間だった」 serves as an introduction leading directly to the dramatic action that follows: the main character starts fighting.
default.q.test-49-q1-1.why.3: ✗ (d) The sudden onset of fatigue was merely the reason the author became sleepy in the preceding context, not the key moment being referred to.
